name: Machinga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Machinga [mvw] is not in the catalog and neither sweep item is about it. Both were tagged to Machinga only by Glottolog's automatic translation of Maho's code P.23 (Makonde). Philippson 1991 (full author PDF from ddl.cnrs.fr, already on file under bemb1257, copied to mach1265 and read) treats Makonde only through Odden's Chimaraba and Chimahuta data: 'langue à accent' with a demarcative accent realized as penultimate lengthening before absolute pause and no vowel-length contrast (pp.356-358, fn.1 p.357; appendix p.507); the word Machinga never occurs in the thesis. Liphola 1992 (LASU proceedings, Maputo) concerns Simakonde = Mozambican Makonde; no open copy exists in any index reachable today (all APIs rate-limited or zero hits), and it is low priority for Machinga. Context already on file (Kraal 2005:25; Leach 2010:9) confirms that no linguist has published data on Chimachinga: Kraal 'we have no data from the other coastal dialect Chimachinga', Leach 'further data is needed'. Nearest described neighbour remains Odden 1990 on Chimaraba (regular penultimate stress + lengthening), which is Makonde, not Machinga. No first-hand statement of Machinga word stress was found; best_new_statement = none. {pdf,txt}, plus access receipts for Liphola 1992.

sources.citation: Odden, David. 1990. Tone in the Makonde dialects: Chimaraba. Studies in African Linguistics 21(1): 61-105, p. 63.
sources.note: NEAREST DESCRIBED NEIGHBOUR ONLY (Chimaraba = the other coastal Makonde dialect, mako1251), not Machinga: 'there are no vowel length contrasts, but due to a regular stress rule, the penultimate syllable of every word is lengthened'; final syllable extraprosodic, stress on penult, Stress Lengthening; utterance-medial lengthening reduced postlexically.

sources.citation: Steere, Edward. 1876. Collections for a handbook of the Makonde language. Zanzibar: UMCA. 71 pp. [Glottolog ref 22558; Glottolog's MED for mach1265, lgcode note 'Rovuma to Lindi = Machinga [mvw]'] — Google Books id 7AK9yCGdaMkC (Harvard copy; = HathiTrust hvd.32044014502942 full view)
sources.note: Nothing. The book opens 'The Makonde language is spoken by the people along the East African coast from the Rovuma to Lindi...' followed by 'THE ALPHABET' (letter values and nasal-prefix alternations only, PP13-PP14), then Substantives p.1, Adjectives, Pronouns, Verbs, word lists, Sentences to p.58. No remark on accent, stress, syllable prominence or length anywhere (full-text scanned grep for accent/stress/penult/syllable/louder: nil; pages inspected).

sources.citation: Leach, Michael B. 2010. Things hold together: foundations for a systemic treatment of verbal and nominal tone in Plateau Shimakonde. LOT 260. Utrecht: LOT. Ch. 1, pp. 8-9.
sources.note: Nothing on Machinga prosody; states that, as for Chimatambwe, no substantive description of Chimachinga exists, that Kraal 2005 places it between the Chimaraba dialect of Makonde and Mwera, that Lorenz 1914 lists it as a Makonde dialect and Harries 1940 as a Mwera dialect, and that 'further data is needed to determine the place of Chimachinga'.

sources.citation: Kraal, Pieter J. 2005. A grammar of Makonde (Chinnima, Tanzania). PhD dissertation, Leiden University. Ch. 2, p. 25.
sources.note: About Machinga only: '(we have no data from the other coastal dialect Chimachinga)'. Kraal's prosodic description is of Chinnima Makonde, not Machinga.
